Amy: Heads-up — onboarding run for llama-3x-8bit hit a perf regression after we applied the HF config change that sets `rope_scaling: {base: 2048, factor: 1.5}`. Latency jumps ~25% at seq_len 1536.

Amy: Profiling points to kernel selection flip: previously used `fast_kv_gemm` path, now we fall back to `matmul_fallback` during KV gather. Log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] kernel_select: model=llama-3x quant=8 seq=1536 heads=32 kv_dim=64 -> selected=matmul_fallback reason=shape_mismatch
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] runtime: copying kv cache to contiguous buffer (size=48MB)
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] perf: token_ms=12.4 (was 9.8 baseline)
```

Jason: @Amy can you paste the HF config we used and the conversion command? suspect safetensors metadata or `num_heads` parsing.

Amy: Sure — conversion:`python convert.py --from=hf --to=redwood --quant=8 --preserve-kv` and HF config snippet: 
```yaml
model_type: llama
hidden_size: 8192
num_attention_heads: 32
rope_scaling: {base: 2048, factor: 1.5}
kv_proj_dim: 2048  # derived, but sometimes missing in some HF exports
```

Vikram: Two quick hypotheses: 1) rope_scaling changed positional embedding expectations causing attention to change codepath that expects different head/kv layout, 2) conversion produced non-contiguous KV tensors triggering fallback.

Marisol: Reproduced locally with the conversion artifacts from the onboarding bucket. Quick perf numbers: seq=512 token_ms=4.2 (ok), seq=1536 token_ms=12.1 (bad). When I force `force_kernel=fast_kv_gemm` token_ms -> 9.9, but result differs slightly on a couple eval prompts (small logits drift).

Jason: That drift suggests we might be using a different KV projection shape (heads*kv_dim mismatch). Can you run `inspect-model --print-kv-layout` on the converted artifact?

Marisol: Ran that, output: 
```
kv_layout: {layers: 32, head_dim: 64, proj_shape: [8192, 2048], contiguous: false}
metadata: {safetensors: true, hf_version: 0.17.3}
```

Vikram: `contiguous: false` is the smoking gun. Our fast kernel requires contiguous KV layout (packed `[layers, seq, heads, head_dim]`). Conversion should set `contiguous=true` or we need a cheap reorder pass during load. Reordering cost might explain the 48MB copy.

Amy: Good catch. Why did this only appear after rope_scaling change?

Vikram: Two possibilities: the conversion has a conditional codepath that packs differently when `rope_scaling` present (we tried to preserve legacy RoPE params). Also HF exports sometimes omit explicit `kv_proj_dim` and we infer it — inference path might choose a different memory layout.

Jason: Plan: (a) add a validation check in onboarding that refuses artifacts with `contiguous:false` unless we run re-pack with measured cost, (b) fix conversion to produce contiguous KV by default, (c) add a perf test that asserts kernel selection doesn't flip for seq in [256,2048].

Amy: +1. For (c) we should add a micro-bench that asserts token_ms delta < 10% vs baseline for quantized artifacts. Marisol can you prototype the re-pack and run accuracy diff?

Marisol: On it. Quick experiment: re-pack (in-place) reduces copy and token_ms at seq=1536 -> 9.6 matching baseline. Accuracy diff: max logit delta 1e-5 on eval set. I'll push a minimal script to the onboarding bucket.

perf-bot: perf/regression alert cleared for artifact `llama-3x-8bit-20260318` after re-pack.

infra-bot: deploy job #6721 triggered: `onboard-validator` will now check `kv_layout.contiguous==true` and `rope_scaling` presence along with `num_attention_heads`/`head_dim` consistency.

Jason: Also add a rule to avoid changing kernel thresholds unless we validate which kernels are selected via `kernel_profiler` for a sweep of seq lengths. We burned time chasing shape vs kernel ambiguity before.

Amy: Agree. I'll open a tiny RFC for the onboarding validator changes + add the micro-bench. Thanks all — major win if re-pack fixes perf without quality loss. :tada:
